category: usenet provider (NNTP access, unlimited data, NL)

free_tier.stated: None. Three paid terms; the 30-day money-back guarantee is the only risk-free route.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a retrieval service, not stored bytes

retention.stated: '6639+ Days Binary Retention' on every plan

egress.terms: 'Unlimited Data', 'Unlimited Speed', '50 Connections', 'No Speed Throttling' on every term. The VPN add-on is EUR 4.99 and is included free on the 15-month term.

tooling: Every usenet client (SABnzbd, NZBGet); 'Free Newsreader with Search' is included on the account.
chaining: The 15-month term at EUR 6.99/month is the cheapest uncapped usenet feed found at EUR 104.85 for the whole term, and it carries a free VPN, which is the egress half of the same stack.

limits.value: an article past retention, or listed by an indexer but never present, answers 423 or 430
the plan's connection count is the ceiling; exceeding it is refused at connect time

identity_cost.detail: Email, password and country at checkout; card payment. No phone or identity document.

reliability_note: No incident found in the pages read. The 52%-off banner has run unchanged since at least 2023-09, which makes it a permanent price rather than an expiring promotion.

evidence.proved: 1 Month EUR 9,50/mo, 12 Months EUR 9,00/mo, 15 Months 'EUR 14,49/mo' struck through and 'EUR 6,99/mo' charged with 'Save 52%', 6639+ days retention, 50 connections, unlimited data
the identical three terms and the identical strike-through, three years earlier
the same deal restated as an aggregate: 'EUR217,35' struck through, 'Now EUR6,99', '52% OFF' - 15 x 14.49

Three stated causes: article older than retention; 'If your NZB was generated by a Usenet Indexer, and that Indexer listed an article that has already expired or never existed'; 'If your newsreader isn't set to subscribe to the newsgroup where the article resides'. Also 'Eweka adds one day of article retention every day'.
EUR 9.50 1 month, EUR 9.00 12 months, EUR 6.99 15-month offer; 6639+ days; 50 connections; unlimited access and speed
Eweka AMS on Highwinds, AS34343, article numbering 'August 2008 - present', NTD law on the Dutch farm; Newshosting AMS listed as a virtual version of the Eweka spool

notes: The largest published promo-versus-list gap in the set: EUR 14.49/month struck through against EUR 6.99 charged, 52%. Two things make it less alarming than the number suggests. The discount has run unchanged for 37 months, so the list price is never observed to be charged; and the 12-month term at EUR 9.00 sets the realistic renewal floor, which is 28.8% above the 15-month rate. A client who renews at the 15-month rate pays nothing extra; one who falls to the 12-month rate pays 28.8% more. All three are named by the vendor. It is recorded as an observation about the documentation, not about the spool. The 15-month offer at EUR 6.99/mo is the lowest per-month figure the vendor itself publishes, at EUR 104.85 for the term.

extras.promo_gap: charged EUR 6.99 against a published list of EUR 14.49: the list is 107.3% higher than the charge; the 12-month term is 28.8% higher
extras.renewal_price: not published; the page shows a struck list and a charged price, and the 12-month term is the nearest published non-promotional rate
extras.account_states: article-level states only on the page read

interface_detail: Access is NNTP over TLS. The schema's interface enum has no nntp token, so this is recorded as unknown; the real interface is the standard usenet protocol.
limits_note: No byte cap on any term. The one number that varies is the connection count, and it does not vary here.
binding_note: Unlimited data and 50 connections with no speed throttle means nothing in the vocabulary fires at 1 TiB/month
confidence_note: Four dated reads, three archived, quoting the same three terms. A paid term would raise it to measured.
